summary: Defines a MIB module for managing ATM-based interfaces, devices, networks and services. It gives SNMP tools standard objects for monitoring and configuring ATM equipment. It obsoletes RFC 1695.

eli5.summary: This is a standard list of dials and gauges for ATM network equipment, so one monitoring program can read them on any maker's gear.

subtitle: The standard SNMP objects for managing ATM interfaces, virtual connections and AAL5 on hosts and switches.

tldr.problem: ATM equipment from different makers needs a common set of SNMP-readable objects so that interfaces, virtual connections and cross-connects can be monitored and configured the same way everywhere.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a MIB module (ATM-MIB) with tables for ATM interface configuration, traffic descriptors, virtual path and channel links, cross-connects and AAL5 connection statistics, and says how to map ATM layers onto MIB-II's ifTable.
tldr.outcome: It replaces RFC 1695 with clarifications for PVCs, SVCs and soft PVCs and a few deprecated objects. Its main purpose is managing ATM permanent virtual connections.

today: RFC 2515 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 1695. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Scope and Purpose
sections.content:
RFC 2515 defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing ATM-based interfaces, devices, networks and services. It replaces RFC 1695, and the changes are summarized in the module's REVISION clause. The module is written in SMIv2, and its Textual Conventions are defined in RFC 2514.

The managed objects cover ATM interfaces, virtual links, cross-connects, AAL5 entities and AAL5 connections in ATM hosts, switches and networks. The memo is primarily about managing ATM PVCs. SVCs are also represented, but full management of SVCs may need capabilities that are out of scope. Managing OAM cell flows and traps for virtual connection or link failures is also outside the scope.

Other MIB modules are still needed alongside this one, for example MIB-II for general system and interface management, and the DS3 or SONET MIBs for physical interfaces.
sections.eli5: This is a rulebook for how ATM network boxes report on themselves, so that monitoring tools can ask any of them the same questions.

sections.title: ATM Concepts the MIB Relies On
sections.content:
An ATM virtual connection is either a Virtual Channel Connection (VCC) or a Virtual Path Connection (VPC). Each is a chain of virtual links (VCLs or VPLs) joined at ATM switches by a cross-connect function. No single device sees the whole connection, so end-to-end management comes from managing each piece. VCCs are bi-directional, but the two directions may have different traffic parameters, and a one-way flow is made by giving zero bandwidth in the other direction.

A PVC is a provisioned connection. An SVC is set up in real time through call set-up signaling. A soft PVC has some switched and some permanent portions.

For traffic management the text covers policing (Usage Parameter Control at a UNI) and shaping, and two Cell Loss Priority values, CLP=0 and CLP=1, where CLP=1 cells are dropped first. It also notes that atmTrafficQoSClass from RFC 1695 is deprecated and replaced by atmServiceCategory.
sections.eli5: Think of a road trip made of several road sections, each run by a different town. A connection is the whole trip, and each link is one section. Permanent ones are fixed roads, switched ones are set up when needed.

sections.title: Structure of the MIB
sections.content:
The objects are grouped into six sets of tables: ATM interface configuration, ATM interface DS3 PLCP and TC sublayer, ATM traffic parameters, virtual link (VPL and VCL) configuration, VP and VC cross-connects, and AAL5 connection performance statistics.

The link tables are used in hosts, switches and networks to create, delete or modify virtual links, and together with the cross-connect tables they manage cross-connects in switches or networks. For a PVC the cross-connect between two VPLs is in atmVpCrossConnectTable and between two VCLs in atmVcCrossConnectTable. For an SVC or soft PVC the cross-connects are in tables of the separate ATM2-MIB, which was still being defined when this RFC was published.

The AAL5 statistics in aal5VccTable are indexed by the AAL5 interface's ifIndex plus VPI and VCI, and hold three counters: CRC errors, SAR time-outs and oversized SDUs.
sections.eli5: The MIB is a set of tables, like spreadsheets: one for each port, one for each link, one for how links are joined, and one for error counts.

sections.title: VPI and VCI Bits: Configured and Negotiated
sections.content:
A manager can configure the maximum number of VPI and VCI bits used on an ATM interface, up to what the hardware supports. These are the Max Active bits. The manager may not control the other end of the link, so the two devices may use ILMI to negotiate Max Current bits, the maximum both interfaces are willing to support.

The text's example: when the two ends are configured with 6 and 8 Max Active VPI bits, both end up with 6 as Max Current. If ILMI negotiation is not supported, the devices have no choice but to use the configured Max Active bits and assume both ends are configured alike.
sections.eli5: Two people choose how many digits to use in a locker number. If one can only handle six and the other eight, they both settle on six.

sections.title: Mapping ATM Layers onto the ifTable
sections.content:
For sysServices in MIB-II, ATM is a data link layer protocol, so ATM switches and networks use the value 2. The ATM cell layer is an entry in the ifTable with ifType 37; its octet counters are the number of cells multiplied by 53, and ifInErrors counts cells dropped due to uncorrectable HEC errors.

The AAL5 CPCS layer entity is also an ifTable entry, with ifType 49. Its error counter covers CRC-32 errors, SAR time-out errors and oversized SDU errors. In a host, AAL5 is stacked directly over the ATM sublayer. In a switch, AAL5 is reached through a proprietary virtual, internal interface (ifType 53) to which the switching fabric directs the AAL5 virtual channels. Per-connection AAL5 statistics come from the AAL5 connection table. AAL3/4 is left to the SMDS MIB, RFC 1694.
sections.eli5: Every layer of the equipment gets its own line on a standard checklist, with a number that says what kind of layer it is.

sections.title: Relationship to the ILMI MIBs
sections.content:
The ILMI MIBs are specified by the ATM Forum. The ILMI protocol and MIBs let two connected ATM Interface Management Entities exchange parameters, mainly to support auto-configuration between ATM peers. The RFC compares which management functions are covered by the ILMI MIBs and which by this memo.

For the information both have in common, every effort was made to keep identical semantics and syntax, even though the objects use different OBJECT IDENTIFIERs.
sections.eli5: There is another group's list of the same dials. This one copies the meanings so the two lists agree, even though the labels are different.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Several objects are read-write or read-create, and allowing SET operations without protection can harm network operations. The objects also expose sensitive information: collectively they allow tracing and influencing virtual connections in ATM switches or networks and reveal their traffic characteristics. So even GET access should be controlled, and values may need encrypting on the wire.

SNMPv1 by itself is not a secure environment, even on a secure network. Implementers are urged to consider SNMPv3, specifically the User-based Security Model (RFC 2274) and the View-based Access Control Model (RFC 2275).
sections.eli5: These dials can change how the network behaves and show who is talking to whom, so only the right people should be allowed to read or turn them.

sections.title: Changes from RFC 1695
sections.content:
The REVISION clause lists the key changes. Textual Conventions and object identities moved to a separate module, and the applicability to PVCs, SVCs and soft PVCs was clarified. DEFVAL clauses were added and the relationship of ifIndex values to ATM layers was clarified.

atmTrafficQosClass was deprecated in favor of atmServiceCategory, and atmInterfaceAddressType and atmInterfaceAdminAddress were deprecated in favor of atmInterfaceSubscrAddress. New items include atmInterfaceCurrentMaxVpiBits and atmInterfaceCurrentMaxVciBits, atmTrafficDescrParamIndexNext, the atmTrafficFrameDiscard capability, connection topology and call control types for links, and aal2 in atmVccAalType.
